content.thinking:
I'm putting together the postmortem and have the key timeline: the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on at 23:06:13. Account page requests started hitting a ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py around 23:06, with the error rate on the account page at 0.50 afterward. Flag evaluations show partial rollout at 23:06 and full on from 23:07.

I'm checking whether the flag-off change ever reached the service, since the logs I have stop before the rollback. The flag was turned off, but the service was still at incident level afterward, so I'm looking for evaluations showing it off after that point and why the errors kept going.

I'm checking whether the flag-off change ever reached the service, since the logs I have stop before the rollback. Errors stayed at incident level after the flag was turned off, so I'm looking at whether the service's evaluations showed it off after that point and why the failures kept going.

I'm weighing whether the flag is really the trigger, since the record says turning it off didn't stop the errors. Still, the errors begin in the same minute the flag starts evaluating as on, so I'll note that switching it off did not end the failures.

I'm settling the mechanism step: the function divides the monthly total by this month's purchase count, which would be zero for shoppers who only bought in earlier months. That reading comes from the code notes alone, so I'm treating the cause as resting on an unrun reading, though the log does show a division by zero at that line.

I'm listing what I ruled out for the cause: the only flag change in the hour before was this one, and the deploy records from the day before the errors show none, so I can cite those reads. I'm also listing contributing factors, starting with the missing pre-enable check on shoppers who bought in earlier months but not this one.

I'm laying out the contributing factors now, starting with the lack of a pre-enable check on shoppers who bought earlier but not this month. The flag went to all traffic at once, with no gradual rollout, so I'm noting that rolling out gradually with an automatic halt on rising error rates would have limited the harm.

I'm weighing whether to include a fallback that renders the account page without the spend summary, since that would have contained the failure. The idea rests on a reading I haven't run, so I'm leaning toward leaving it out. A separate gap stands out: the alert went out with no link to an on-call incident, so nobody was paged and the fix stayed waiting.

I'm checking what would actually stop the harm now that turning the flag off didn't end it, and how to confirm the fix at the service rather than assuming it.

I'm settling how the fix gets confirmed at the service: turning the flag off again and checking that the evaluation lines read off and the account-page error rate drops back toward its earlier level. Separately, I want to find out whether the service's evaluations actually read off between the later two timestamps, and if they did, why the account page kept failing.

I'm drafting the action items now: a pre-enable test for the no-purchases-this-month edge case, a gradual rollout with an automatic halt on rising errors, and paging on-call for the high error rate alert on io-shop.

I'm settling what has to change before the account page stops failing: the flag stayed on with the division-by-zero fault still in the code, so account page requests could keep failing with that error for as long as monthly-spend-feature is enabled. Shoppers' account pages failed to load as a result of that error.

I'm writing up the root cause: a function in the spend summary module divides the month's total spend by the count of this month's purchases with no zero guard, so shoppers with earlier purchases but none this month hit a ZeroDivisionError.

I'm working out the causal chain now, starting with the account page errors that the alert picked up.

I'm tracing the causal chain: account page requests failed with a ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, starting the minute the monthly-spend-feature flag was switched on, when only a single client-disconnect error had been logged before. Service evaluations went from all off to mostly on during that change and fully on afterward, and the errors began in the same minute. I'm ruling out the deploys and the other flag changes, since none of them match that window.

I'm writing the step on the flag-on change: the account page started failing right after the flag went on, and I'm noting that no earlier change in the record was read, so nothing else was ruled out there. The last step will say in one sentence that the path the flag turns on divides by this month's purchase count, which fails for shoppers who bought earlier but not this month, leaving the detail to the root cause.

I'm noting what went well in the response: the onset was placed at 23:06, matching the flag change, and the Investigator found both the flag change and the ZeroDivisionError lines. Now I'm turning to what went wrong, starting with the Mitigation Agent's judgment that the flag revert was refuted without the service's post-revert evaluations or log lines being read.

I'm checking whether the second investigation's log read covered the minutes after the revert, since it only reached back to 23:09. The re-proposed flag cause was already refuted, so that pass added nothing new to try.

I'm noting the working assumption that the service-wide error rise comes from account page failures, based on the account-page error-rate lines matching the service's overall rate; no per-route breakdown was read to confirm it.

I'm making sure I don't include any figures in the write-up, so I'll describe the error rate as high rather than quoting numbers, and check the remaining sentences of the draft for any stray numbers.

action_items.item: Before any io-shop feature flag is switched on in production, require tests of the code path it enables that cover empty and edge-case account data, such as an account with past purchases but none this month.
Roll out io-shop feature flag changes gradually, and halt the rollout automatically when the service's error rate rises.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to the on-call rotation so that it pages a person.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed: the service logged a high account-page error rate every minute after the onset, and the service-wide error rate rose above its alert threshold.
Account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError in the spend summary code, starting in the onset minute. In the minute before, the only failure logged was a single shopper closing the connection.

ruled_out.what: A deploy: when the production change events were read, no deploy came back, only flag changes to monthly-spend-feature.
Another flag change: in the hour before, the flag provider's history showed only this one flag change by anyone but Argus.

causal_chain.step: An admin switched monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. The service's flag evaluations went from all off in the minute before, to mostly on in the minute of the change, to all on after it. The division-by-zero failures began in that same minute. The changes read for the day before the onset held no earlier change, so there was no earlier change to rule out.

The path the flag turns on works out this month's average spend per item by dividing by the number of purchases made this month, and according to Code-Fix's reading that number is zero for shoppers who have bought before but not this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Switching on a new monthly-spend feature made the account page run a calculation that likely divides by the number of purchases made this month, and that breaks for shoppers who have bought before but not yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Before monthly-spend-feature was switched on in production, no check or test was seen that ran the path it turns on against an account with past purchases but none this month.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have shown up before the flag reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag change reached almost all of the service's evaluations within the minute it was made. No gradual rollout and no automatic halt on a rise in errors was seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have hit the failing path before the rise in errors stopped the rollout.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: The HighErrorRate alert on io-shop paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have been on the incident when Argus ran out of explanations to try, and could have acted on the open fault sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident in the same minute the flag was switched on.
The Investigator Agent tied the failures to the monthly-spend-feature change and the ZeroDivisionError log lines.
The Mitigation Agent reverted the flag. The action could be put back.
The Mitigation Agent put the flag back on once it judged that the revert had not helped, leaving the service as it found it.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request for a person to review.

went_wrong: When the Investigator Agent investigated again, it put forward only the same flag change the revert had already been judged against, so Argus had nothing new to try.

input.root_cause: In src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, `average_spend_per_item_this_month` divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases flagged as this month and does not guard against zero. For a shopper who has bought before but not yet this month, it raises ZeroDivisionError at line {F1.1}. That function sits on the path the monthly-spend-feature flag turns on, so the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: Account page requests from shoppers with no purchases this month could keep failing with a division-by-zero error for as long as monthly-spend-feature stays on and the code is unchanged.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again. Confirm at the service that its log lines show the flag evaluating off, that the ZeroDivisionError lines from spend_summary.py stop, and that the account-page error rate falls back towards the baseline of {errors_before}.
input.symptom: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out whether the service's own evaluations of monthly-spend-feature read off between the flag being switched off at {P2.1} and back on at {P3.1}. If they did, find out why account page requests kept failing anyway.
